text:
Mark Scheifele has spent his career being underrated, and he is running out of franchise records to take. On Saturday he tied the Vegas game 3-3 and, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger noted, passed Dale Hawerchuk for the most goals in Jets history. The Jets lost that one in a shootout, but the week still belonged to him: three assists Thursday, a record Saturday. Kyle Connor has 18 goals. This is also the first Winnipeg season after Connor Hellebuyck, and Dawson Mercer, now a Jet, has been one of the most written-about players on the roster this month.

The numbers underneath are shakier. Winnipeg takes 47% of the five-on-five expected goals (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and our numbers give the Jets a 26% playoff chance despite 26 points. Stuart Skinner starts at .883, 1.7 goals saved above expected. Dylan DeMelo is among the absent. Alex Iafallo is one point from 300.

Utah is the better team on chances, at 57% of the five-on-five expected goals, and arrives off a 3-2 win over Anaheim that Logan Cooley settled with 1:17 left. Cooley has 14 points in his last ten and has had a loud week otherwise: Gabriel Landeskog was fined for cross-checking him, and Jack McBain answered by fighting Landeskog, in a Colorado rivalry that, in the Denver Post's words, has found some bad blood. Clayton Keller and Dylan Guenther are both cleared from the injury report, which would put most of the top six back together, though Nick Schmaltz and John Marino are still out. Sebastian Cossa starts in place of Karel Vejmelka, at .887 and 3.6 goals below expected in ten games. Barrett Hayton and Kailer Yamamoto are our Sleepers.

Our numbers see this as close, 3.46 expected goals for Utah to 3.30 for Winnipeg.
headline: Scheifele's record, and Cooley at full speed
